bagCoatingTypes.name: Legacy Long-Chain PFAS Coating (C8 / 8:2 FTOH & PAPs Surfactants)
bagCoatingTypes.chemicalClass: Polyfluoroalkyl Phosphate Esters (PAPs) & 8:2 Fluorotelomer Alcohols (8:2 FTOH / PFOA)
bagCoatingTypes.regulatoryStatus: Banned/Phased out in US (2016), but found in legacy supplies & unregulated imports
bagCoatingTypes.description: Historic grease-proofing formulation used extensively from 1990 to 2016. Employs polyfluoroalkyl phosphate esters that prevent boiling oil bleed-through. Under high microwave susceptor temperatures (200°C–230°C), thermal cleavage releases free PFOA and volatile 8:2 FTOH directly into molten butterfat and steam.

bagCoatingTypes.name: Short-Chain PFAS Substitute (C6 / 6:2 FTOH & PFHxA Surfactants)
bagCoatingTypes.chemicalClass: 6:2 Fluorotelomer Alcohols (6:2 FTOH), diPAPs & Perfluorohexanoic Acid (PFHxA)
bagCoatingTypes.regulatoryStatus: Voluntarily phased out by US FDA in 2024; still widely used in global markets
bagCoatingTypes.iarcClassification: Category 2B / Under active review (precursor to persistent 5:3 and 6:2 acids)
bagCoatingTypes.description: Marketed as a safer replacement for PFOA. While PFHxA eliminates faster from human blood than PFOA (half-life ~32 days), 6:2 FTOH has higher vapor pressure at 200°C, causing 2x to 3x higher volatile emissions into the microwave steam chamber during popping.

bagCoatingTypes.name: Certified PFAS-Free Parchment / Silicone-Calendered Kraft Paper
bagCoatingTypes.chemicalClass: Mechanical Supercalendered Cellulose with Cross-Linked Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)
bagCoatingTypes.regulatoryStatus: 100% Compliant with FDA 2024 Food Paper Ban & EU REACH
bagCoatingTypes.description: Clean modern packaging technology utilizing ultra-dense mechanical fiber calendering and vegetable silicone coatings. Achieves grease resistance without any fluorochemical surfactants, yielding zero PFAS migration into food or vapor outgassing.

bagCoatingTypes.name: Uncoated Natural Brown Kraft Paper (DIY Lunch Bag Popcorn)
bagCoatingTypes.chemicalClass: 100% Unbleached Virgin Kraft Wood Pulp (Zero Added Coatings)
bagCoatingTypes.description: Standard untreated brown grocery bag used for home microwave popping. Has lower lipid holdout (hot butter can seep through paper fibers), but completely eliminates all fluorochemical surfactants, plasticizers, and metallic susceptor films.

fatMatrices.name: Extra Movie Theater Butter (Hydrogenated Palm Oil & Butterfat, 32g Fat)
fatMatrices.description: Heavy lipid load. Molten trans-fats and palm oil form a boiling puddle directly over the vacuum-metallized susceptor pad, acting as an aggressive lipophilic solvent that extracts up to 85% of soluble fluorochemicals from the paper substrate.

fatMatrices.name: Standard Butter / Vegetable Oil (Palm & Soybean Oil Blend, 16g Fat)
fatMatrices.description: Typical commercial supermarket popcorn bag. Moderate fat reservoir coats the majority of expanding popcorn kernels and paper wall margins during rotational agitation.

fatMatrices.name: Light / Low-Fat Style (Minimal Palm Olein Oil, 5g Fat)
fatMatrices.description: Reduced fat formulation. Lower lipid volume limits liquid phase chemical extraction, though high steam generation still drives volatile fluorotelomer alcohol vaporization.

fatMatrices.name: Dry / Zero Added Fat (Kernels Only, ~1g Natural Kernel Oil)
fatMatrices.description: Popcorn popped without added oils. Chemical migration into the edible portion is restricted to direct physical contact with hot paper surfaces, drastically reducing oral lipid uptake.

poppingTimeProfiles.name: Fast / Under-Popped (105 seconds / 1:45 min)
poppingTimeProfiles.description: Short cycle. Susceptor barely reaches peak operating temperature; lower PFAS degradation and chemical extraction, but leaves 25%+ unpopped kernels.

poppingTimeProfiles.name: Standard Optimal Popping (150 seconds / 2:30 min)
poppingTimeProfiles.description: Recommended cooking duration on 1000W microwaves (1–2 seconds between pops). Full bag expansion; susceptor pad reaches 200°C–215°C, triggering peak fluorotelomer partitioning into molten lipids.

poppingTimeProfiles.name: Overheated / Scorched (195 seconds / 3:15 min)
poppingTimeProfiles.description: Dangerous overcooking. Kernels scorch and charred oil burns onto paper. High susceptor heat (>230°C) accelerates thermal pyrolysis of paper sizing polymers, dramatically increasing toxic fluorinated gas outgassing.

bagOpeningInhalationProfiles.name: Immediate Bag Tear Over Face (<5 sec post-beep, Inhaling Steam Plume)
bagOpeningInhalationProfiles.diacetylCoExposure: Severe (High airborne diacetyl butter flavor concentration)
bagOpeningInhalationProfiles.description: Worst-case inhalation scenario. Consumer tears bag open right in front of face immediately upon removing from microwave. Direct blast of 90°C–95°C steam carries volatile 6:2/8:2 FTOH aerosols directly into nasal and bronchial airways.

bagOpeningInhalationProfiles.name: Arm's Length Countertop Opening (15 sec wait, Pointing Away)
bagOpeningInhalationProfiles.description: Typical cautious handling. Bag is placed on countertop and pulled open facing away. The high-concentration steam jet dilutes into room volume, reducing direct peak inhalation dose by ~65%.

bagOpeningInhalationProfiles.name: Vented / Cooled Wait (60+ sec rest before opening)
bagOpeningInhalationProfiles.diacetylCoExposure: Minimal (Vapor condensed on interior paper walls)
bagOpeningInhalationProfiles.description: Safest handling protocol. Waiting 60–90 seconds allows internal steam to cool below 60°C. Volatile fluorotelomers condense back onto interior paper and oil, reducing airborne inhalation exposure by >90%.

cleanPoppingAlternatives.name: Food-Grade Tempered Platinum Silicone Microwave Popper Bowl
cleanPoppingAlternatives.description: The gold-standard microwave alternative. Heat-resistant up to 230°C (450°F), collapsible for easy drawer storage, requires no oil or butter to pop, and eliminates 100% of single-use disposable packaging waste.

cleanPoppingAlternatives.name: Electric Countertop Hot Air Vortex Popper
cleanPoppingAlternatives.description: Dedicated appliance using high-velocity heated air to circulate and pop kernels with zero cooking oil. Completely eliminates fluorinated paper, susceptor films, and lipid oxidation.

cleanPoppingAlternatives.name: 304 Stainless Steel Hand-Crank Stovetop Popper (Whirley-Pop)
cleanPoppingAlternatives.oilRequirement: 1–2 tbsp healthy oil (Avocado, Coconut, or Ghee)
cleanPoppingAlternatives.description: Heavy-duty stainless steel pot with manual stirring paddles that prevent kernel burning. Allows cooking with high-stability healthy fats (ghee, extra-virgin olive, or avocado oil) with zero chemical outgassing.

cleanPoppingAlternatives.name: DIY Uncoated Brown Paper Lunch Bag Popcorn
cleanPoppingAlternatives.description: Cost-effective hack using standard brown paper lunch sacks folded over twice (without metal staples). Completely free of fluoropolymers and susceptors, though requires careful supervision to prevent scorching.

scientificReferences.citation: Begley, T. H., et al. (2005). Migration of fluorochemical paper additives from food-contact paper into foods and food simulants. Food Additives and Contaminants, 22(10), 1023-1031.
scientificReferences.finding: Demonstrated that 65% to 85% of polyfluoroalkyl phosphate esters in microwave popcorn paper migrate into molten oil matrices during standard popping.

scientificReferences.citation: D'eon, J. C., & Mabury, S. A. (2011). Is indirect exposure a significant contributor to the burden of perfluorinated acids observed in humans? Environmental Science & Technology, 45(19), 7974-7984.
scientificReferences.finding: Identified fluorotelomer alcohol (FTOH) volatiles in popcorn bag steam as significant precursors that metabolize into persistent PFOA and PFHxA in human blood.

scientificReferences.citation: European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) CONTAM Panel. (2020). Risk to human health related to the presence of perfluoroalkyl substances in food. EFSA Journal, 18(9), e06223.
scientificReferences.finding: Established the Tolerable Weekly Intake (TWI) of 4.4 ng/kg body weight per week for the sum of four PFAS (PFOA, PFNA, PFHxS, PFOS), driven by immunotoxicity.

scientificReferences.citation: US Food and Drug Administration (FDA). (2024). FDA Announces PFAS Substances No Longer Used in Food Packaging.
scientificReferences.finding: Finalized voluntary manufacturer phase-out of remaining grease-proofing PFAS paper substances in the US market as of February 2024.
